title: How a Screen Works
objective: After this level you can explain pixels and how a screen mixes red, green and blue light.
summary: A screen is a grid of pixels, about 2 million on HD. Red, green and blue light fool the eye's three cone types. An LCD passes or blocks a backlight.

cards.headline: Your screen has no yellow in it. So how does it show you a banana?
cards.body: Look closely enough at a color screen and you won't find yellow, orange or pink. Every pixel is built from just three colors: red, green and blue. The whole trick of a screen is how few colors it takes to fool your eye.

cards.headline: Pixels: pictures made of dots
cards.body: A pixel is the smallest unit of a screen image, with its own brightness and color. Millions sit in a grid, and from a normal distance your eye blends them into one smooth picture. An HD screen is 1,920 pixels across and 1,080 down: about 2 million. A 4K screen has four times as many, about 8.3 million. Level 46's camera sensor has pixels too: there they catch light, and here they give it out.

cards.headline: Three colors fool your eye
cards.body: Your eye senses color with three types of cone cells, each most sensitive to a different range of wavelengths, roughly red, green and blue. So a screen only needs those three lights. Each pixel holds red, green and blue subpixels, and mixing light adds up: red plus green looks yellow, and all three together look white. Vary how bright each one glows, and you get a broad range of hues.

mascot.line: No yellow anywhere: your banana is red and green light, side by side.

cards.headline: An LCD is a wall of tiny shutters
cards.body: An LCD makes no light of its own. A backlight shines from behind, and each subpixel has liquid crystals that change how much light gets through when a voltage is applied, behind a red, green or blue filter. Level 5's LEDs make light directly; these crystals only let it pass or block it. The screen is less a lamp than a window with millions of tiny blinds.

cards.headline: Screens: lit
learned: A pixel is the smallest unit of a screen image
HD is about 2 million pixels; 4K has four times as many
Red, green and blue light mix to make other colors
An LCD's crystals let a backlight through or block it

questions.prompt: About how many pixels does a 1,920 by 1,080 HD screen have?

options.label: About 2 thousand
options.rationale: Far too few: that's one row plus a bit.

options.label: About 200 thousand
options.rationale: Multiply 1,920 by 1,080 for the full count.

questions.explanation: 1,920 x 1,080 is about 2 million pixels; a 4K screen has four times as many.

questions.prompt: A screen shows a yellow banana with no yellow subpixels at all. How?

options.label: It shines red and green light together
It mixes blue and orange paint in each pixel
It uses a special yellow backlight
options.rationale: The trick is mixing red and green light.

questions.explanation: Mixing light adds up: red plus green light looks yellow to the eye's three kinds of cones.

questions.prompt: Level 5's LEDs make their own light. How is an LCD screen different?

options.label: It heats a filament behind each pixel
Its crystals only let a backlight through or block it
It makes light from a chemical reaction, like a battery
options.rationale: No chemistry: the crystals act as shutters.

options.label: It has no pixels, just one big light

questions.explanation: An LCD makes no light of its own; its liquid crystals control how much backlight passes through each colored subpixel.
